l: Dandy Dick, Dandy Dick, DANDY DICK. / THE FIRST ACT.
s: Salome Jedd and Sheba Jedd plan to attend the Fancy Dress Masked Ball at Durnstone secretly with Gerald Tarver and Nugent Darbey, but they are alarmed by the expensive account for their fancy dresses. Dr. Jedd discovers their financial request and explains that the family must retrench because he has no spare cash and has committed £1,000 to the restoration of the Minister Spire. Dr. Jedd also announces that his widowed sister, Georgiana Tidman, is coming to live at the Deanery of St. Marvells, and she unexpectedly arrives after staying at Durnstone.

l: Salome, Dandy Dick, DANDY DICK. / THE FIRST ACT.
s: Salome Jedd plans to attend the Fancy Dress Masked Ball at Durnstone secretly with Gerald Tarver. She worries about the cost of her French Revolution costume, asks Dr. Jedd for money, and learns that the family must retrench.

l: Sheba, Dandy Dick, DANDY DICK. / THE FIRST ACT.
s: Sheba Jedd plans to attend the Fancy Dress Masked Ball with Nugent Darbey and is distressed by the cost of her flower-girl costume. She joins Salome in asking Dr. Jedd for money and reacts angrily to the news that Georgiana Tidman will come to live with them.

l: Dr. Jedd, Dandy Dick, DANDY DICK. / THE FIRST ACT.
s: Dr. Jedd, the Dean of St. Marvells, learns that Salome and Sheba want money for their dresses and tells them that he has no spare cash. He explains that he has subscribed £1,000 to the restoration of the Minister Spire, conditional on seven other donors contributing the same amount, and announces that Georgiana Tidman will live with the family.

l: Major Tarver, Dandy Dick, DANDY DICK. / THE FIRST ACT.
s: Gerald Tarver visits the Deanery with Nugent Darbey to arrange the evening's plans and has arranged the girls' costumes. He is described as a middle-aged officer with an unstable liver, alternating between excitement and depression, and intends to appear as Charles the First at the ball.

l: Mr. Darbey, Dandy Dick, DANDY DICK. / THE FIRST ACT.
s: Nugent Darbey visits the Deanery with Gerald Tarver and helps arrange the girls' attendance at the ball. He is described as a young, pompous officer who intends to appear as Charles the Martyr.

l: Georgiana, Dandy Dick, DANDY DICK. / THE FIRST ACT.
s: Georgiana Tidman is Dr. Jedd's widowed sister and is coming to live at the Deanery of St. Marvells. Dr. Jedd says that she continued her late husband's career as a horse-breeder and gentleman jockey, became known as the Daisy of the Turf, and eventually lost her horses and property.

l: the Deanery, Dandy Dick, DANDY DICK. / THE FIRST ACT.
s: The Deanery of St. Marvells is the home of Dr. Jedd, Salome, and Sheba. Gerald Tarver and Nugent Darbey visit it to arrange the ball plans, and Georgiana Tidman is expected to move there.

l: Durnstone, Dandy Dick, DANDY DICK. / THE FIRST ACT.
s: Durnstone is the place where the Fancy Dress Masked Ball is being held and where Gerald Tarver and Nugent Darbey are stationed. Georgiana Tidman stayed there at the Wheatsheaf before coming to the Deanery.

l: Fancy Dress Masked Ball at Durnstone, Dandy Dick, DANDY DICK. / THE FIRST ACT.
s: The Fancy Dress Masked Ball at Durnstone is promoted by the officers of the Hussars and is scheduled for that night. Salome and Sheba intend to attend secretly with Gerald Tarver and Nugent Darbey.

l: the scandalous costumes, Dandy Dick, DANDY DICK. / THE FIRST ACT.
s: The fancy dresses are being made in London from Salome and Sheba's brown paper patterns. Salome's costume is a French Revolution gown and Sheba's is a flower-girl skirt and bodice; the dresses arrive in a hamper labeled as cast-off clothing.

l: the account for the fancy dresses, Dandy Dick, DANDY DICK. / THE FIRST ACT.
s: The account for the fancy dresses totals forty pounds, nineteen shillings and demands cash payment. It includes fifteen guineas for Salome's gown, ten guineas for Sheba's costume, additional charges for trimmings and extras, and a note that the girls' brown paper patterns were mislaid.

l: retrenchment, Dandy Dick, DANDY DICK. / THE FIRST ACT.
s: Dr. Jedd says that the family's spending on clothes and other bills must be stopped and summarizes the solution as 'Retrench and Rejoice.' He hopes Georgiana Tidman will help impose the precepts of retrenchment.

l: the family finances, Dandy Dick, DANDY DICK. / THE FIRST ACT.
s: The family finances are strained by £156, 18 shillings and 3 pence in existing bills and by the costly dresses. Dr. Jedd says that he can immediately command considerably under £500, while he has pledged £1,000 to the Minister Spire restoration fund if seven other donors match it.

l: Dandy Dick, Dandy Dick, _GEORGIANA TIDMAN enters.
s: Georgiana Tidman arrives at the Deanery and reveals herself as a former racehorse owner known as George Tidd, to Augustin's embarrassment. Sir Tristram Mardon visits to discuss the races at St. Marvells and reveals that he co-owns Dandy Dick with Georgiana, who secretly intends to bet on the horse. Salome and Sheba disclose that they owe forty pounds, nineteen shillings and ask Georgiana to help them win the money. Georgiana agrees to place their petticoats on Dandy Dick, ending the act with the girls frightened by the risk.

Georgiana arrives at the Deanery dressed in pronounced masculine style and behaving in a jovial, horsey manner. She explains that she was formerly known as George Tidd, a racing figure whose colors were crimson and black diamonds, and that she owns half of Dandy Dick through an arrangement with John Fielder. She agrees to bet on Dandy Dick and encourages Salome and Sheba to stake their money on him.

l: Dr. Jedd, Dandy Dick, _GEORGIANA TIDMAN enters.
s: Augustin is shocked and embarrassed by Georgiana's manners, racing language, and public connection with horse racing. He hopes that the serene atmosphere of the Deanery will change her, but becomes increasingly disturbed when Sir Tristram and Georgiana discuss racing and Dandy Dick. He also worries about the effect of Georgiana's arrival before the races at St. Marvells.

Salome welcomes Georgiana despite not understanding all of her racing language. She and Sheba reveal that they are in debt and ask Georgiana to help them win enough money to pay it. Salome agrees to put their money on Dandy Dick.

Sheba quickly takes a liking to Georgiana and describes herself and Salome as 'weary fragments' who are everything except chastened widows. She reveals that the girls owe forty pounds, nineteen shillings and asks Georgiana to help them win the money through Dandy Dick. She joins Salome in accepting Georgiana's betting plan.

l: Sir Tristram, Dandy Dick, _GEORGIANA TIDMAN enters.
s: Sir Tristram visits Augustin and enthusiastically discusses the races, especially Dandy Dick's prospects in the Durnstone Handicap. He reveals that he is a half-owner of Dandy Dick and is delighted to discover that Georgiana, formerly George Tidd, owns the other half. He leaves after agreeing with Georgiana that Dandy Dick is fit and likely to win.

l: the Deanery, Dandy Dick, _GEORGIANA TIDMAN enters.
s: The Deanery receives Georgiana as Augustin's widowed sister and becomes the setting for her reunion with Augustin and Sir Tristram. Georgiana jokes that if she remains there until the autumn meeting, the Canons and the Bishop may be found lunching with her on the hill.

l: St. Marvells, Dandy Dick, _GEORGIANA TIDMAN enters.
s: St. Marvells is the place where the races are about to take place. Augustin is concerned that Georgiana has arrived at the Deanery on the eve of the races there.

l: Dandy Dick, Dandy Dick, _GEORGIANA TIDMAN enters.
s: Dandy Dick is Sir Tristram's racehorse, entered in the Durnstone Handicap with Tom Gallawood up. Sir Tristram says the horse is fit, shining, and not carrying too much or too little weight, while Georgiana declares that she knows the horse thoroughly and expects him to win. Georgiana reveals that she owns half of him and decides to bet on him.

l: Durnstone Handicap, Dandy Dick, _GEORGIANA TIDMAN enters.
s: The Durnstone Handicap is the race in which Dandy Dick is entered for the following day. Sir Tristram gives Dandy Dick's weight as nine stone two and names Tom Gallawood as his rider.

l: St. Marvells Spring Meeting, Dandy Dick, _GEORGIANA TIDMAN enters.
s: The races at St. Marvells are scheduled for the following day and are a source of anxiety for Augustin because of Georgiana's racing interests. Georgiana and Sir Tristram discuss Dandy Dick's chances in connection with them.

l: horse racing, Dandy Dick, _GEORGIANA TIDMAN enters.
s: Horse racing has been a major part of Georgiana's past and remains an interest she cannot abandon. She says that she cannot live without horseflesh and continues to understand racing form, colors, stables, and betting despite promising Augustin that she would not own anything on four legs.

l: betting on Dandy Dick, Dandy Dick, _GEORGIANA TIDMAN enters.
s: Georgiana decides to bet every penny she has on Dandy Dick after judging that he is fit to win. She then agrees to let Salome and Sheba stake their limited money on him in hopes of covering their debt.

l: the thousand-pound wager, Dandy Dick, _GEORGIANA TIDMAN enters.
s: Georgiana says that if she is not a richer woman by a thousand pounds the following night, she will have had a bad day. She also jokingly offers to make a thousand-sovereign wager concerning her position in the Deanery.

l: the account for the fancy dresses, Dandy Dick, _GEORGIANA TIDMAN enters.
s: Salome and Sheba disclose that they owe forty pounds, nineteen shillings without Augustin's knowledge. They say they have only fifteen shillings and threepence of their own and ask Georgiana to help them win enough money to pay what they owe.

l: Dandy Dick, Dandy Dick, THE SECOND ACT.
s: After dinner at the Deanery, Sheba and Salome plan to leave secretly while Georgiana jokes about the meal, the guests, and horse racing. Major Tarver fails to sing because his music is missing, while Mr. Darbey plays the violin with Sheba accompanying him. The Dean learns that his thousand-pound Restoration Fund offer has prompted seven wealthy donors to give a thousand pounds each, leaving him responsible for the offer. When the Swan Inn catches fire, Dandy Dick is rescued and Georgiana insists on bringing him into the Deanery stables, before Mr. Darbey briefly returns for his violin and provokes the Dean further.

l: Sheba, Dandy Dick, THE SECOND ACT.
s: Sheba plans with Salome to leave the Deanery secretly through the front door and return through a window. She accompanies Mr. Darbey's violin playing, worries that the Dean is in the way, and helps send the evening's guests away.

l: Salome, Dandy Dick, THE SECOND ACT.
s: Salome joins Sheba's plan to leave the Deanery secretly and discusses the successful dinner. She sits with the distressed Major Tarver, helps arrange his proposed singing, and later helps dismiss him and Mr. Darbey.

l: Georgiana, Dandy Dick, THE SECOND ACT.
s: Georgiana serves tea, mocks the dinner and the male guests, and studies her betting book. When the Swan Inn burns, she rushes to help rescue the horses, learns that Dandy Dick is safe but has a singed tail, and insists on bringing him into the Deanery stables.

l: Dr. Jedd, Dandy Dick, THE SECOND ACT.
s: The Dean is distressed by Mr. Darbey and anxious about the newspaper's report on his thousand-pound offer to the Restoration Fund. He learns that seven wealthy people have each offered a thousand pounds, then becomes alarmed when the Swan Inn burns and Georgiana proposes housing Dandy Dick at the Deanery. He nearly behaves rudely toward Mr. Darbey and later chases after him to offer an explanation.

l: Mr. Darbey, Dandy Dick, THE SECOND ACT.
s: Mr. Darbey patronizes the Dean, argues with him about an army question, and plays his violin while Sheba accompanies him. He resents Major Tarver's singing ambitions, later invites the Dean to visit him, and returns to retrieve his violin after the Dean declares that he will not see him again.

l: Major Tarver, Dandy Dick, THE SECOND ACT.
s: Major Tarver suffers from indigestion after dinner and jokes about needing charcoal biscuits in battle. He intends to sing "Come into the garden, Maud," but discovers that his music is missing, then leaves with Mr. Darbey after the Swan Inn fire is brought under control.

l: Sir Tristram, Dandy Dick, THE SECOND ACT.
s: Sir Tristram Mardon reports that Dandy Dick has been rescued safely from the Swan Inn, though the horse's tail is singed and two pails of cold water were thrown over him. He agrees with Georgiana that Dandy Dick should be brought into the Deanery stables and leaves with her to arrange it.

l: Dandy Dick, Dandy Dick, THE SECOND ACT.
s: Dandy Dick is rescued from the burning Swan Inn safe and sound, but with part of his tail singed. He is being run up and down the lane to get warm after cold water was thrown over him, and Georgiana plans to put him in the Deanery stables.

l: the Deanery, Dandy Dick, THE SECOND ACT.
s: The Deanery hosts the dinner and evening gathering, where the guests drink tea, listen to violin playing, and react to the Restoration Fund news. Georgiana proposes using its stables as shelter for Dandy Dick after the Swan Inn fire.

l: the Swan Inn, Dandy Dick, THE SECOND ACT.
s: The Swan Inn catches fire during the evening. Its horses are cleared out, and Dandy Dick is rescued before Georgiana proposes moving him to the Deanery stables.

l: the Restoration Fund, Dandy Dick, THE SECOND ACT.
s: The Restoration Fund receives the benefit of the Dean's public thousand-pound offer. The offer prompts seven wealthy people, including three brewers, to come forward with a thousand pounds each.

l: the Minister Spire, Dandy Dick, THE SECOND ACT.
s: The Minster Spire is described as being somewhat out of repair and in need of restoration. The Dean's concern for it leads him to make his thousand-pound offer.

l: the dinner, Dandy Dick, THE SECOND ACT.
s: The dinner at the Deanery is called a success, although the mutton is overdone, the potatoes rattle, the custards are a first attempt, and the chimney appears to need sweeping. The guests are mostly silent, and the women jokingly describe it as a frightfully jolly dinner.

l: the fire at the Swan Inn, Dandy Dick, THE SECOND ACT.
s: The Swan Inn fire appears as a bright red conflagration in the sky and interrupts the music at the Deanery. It leads to the rescue of Dandy Dick and Georgiana's decision to shelter him at the Deanery.

l: the Restoration Fund offer, Dandy Dick, THE SECOND ACT.
s: The Dean's offer of a thousand pounds to the Restoration Fund produces the desired result: seven wealthy people each offer a thousand pounds toward restoring the Minster Spire. The Dean is then obliged to pay his own thousand pounds and is distressed by the consequence.

l: Durnstone Handicap, Dandy Dick, THE SECOND ACT.
s: Georgiana believes Dandy Dick has backed himself to win the handicap. She worries that the cold water thrown over him may have harmed his chances, but treats his singed tail as less weight for him to carry.

l: Dandy Dick, Dandy Dick, GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM enter by the window.
s: Georgiana and Sir Tristram shelter Dandy Dick at the Deanery after the fire at the Swan, while Hatcham fears the fire may have been deliberate and aimed at the horse. Georgiana urges the Dean to raise fifty pounds by betting on Dandy Dick in the handicap race, and the Dean eventually gives Edward Blore the money to place the bet. Blore admits that he has gambled at races, including on commission for the kitchen, and secretly adds strychnine to the bolus the Dean prepares for Dandy Dick. The Dean, Georgiana, and Sir Tristram each become anxious about Dandy Dick during the storm, while unidentified people approach the Deanery garden.

l: Georgiana, Dandy Dick, GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM enter by the window.
s: Georgiana helps shelter Dandy Dick in the Deanery stables and encourages Sir Tristram not to despair over the horse's injured tail. She urges the Dean to bet fifty pounds on Dandy Dick in the handicap race to help pay for the Spire, then orders Blore to prepare food and champagne for the horse's party on the Hill. During the storm, she prepares to sit with Dandy Dick because she fears for him.

l: Sir Tristram, Dandy Dick, GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM enter by the window.
s: Sir Tristram enters the Deanery with Georgiana and worries about Dandy Dick's tail. He is given accommodation in Sheba's old nursery and later meets Georgiana during the storm, when they hear people moving in the garden and hide to watch them.

l: Dr. Jedd, Dandy Dick, GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM enter by the window.
s: The Dean objects to Dandy Dick and Sir Tristram remaining at the Deanery but is unable to prevent it. Facing bills connected with the threatened Spire, he is tempted by Georgiana's proposal to bet fifty pounds on Dandy Dick and gives Blore the money to place the wager. He then prepares a veterinary bolus for Dandy Dick, while believing he is acting humanely and not seeking to give the horse an unfair advantage.

l: Dandy Dick, Dandy Dick, GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM enter by the window.
s: Dandy Dick is sheltered in the Deanery stables after the fire at the Swan and is reported to be feeding steadily. He has lost his tail and may have suffered a chill, but Georgiana and others expect him to compete in the handicap race. Unbeknownst to the Dean, Blore adds strychnine to the bolus prepared for him.

l: Blore, Dandy Dick, GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM enter by the window.
s: Edward Blore admits that he has gambled at races on his own account and on commission for the kitchen, and he gives the Dean a tip that Bonny Betsy will win the handicap. After receiving the Dean's fifty pounds to bet on Dandy Dick, he secretly adds strychnine to the bolus intended for the horse.

l: the Deanery, Dandy Dick, GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM enter by the window.
s: The Deanery shelters Dandy Dick in its stables and Sir Tristram in the old nursery. Georgiana announces that smoking is permitted throughout the house, and the Dean fears that the horse, gambling, and Georgiana's behavior are contaminating its formerly respectable peace.

l: the Minister Spire, Dandy Dick, GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM enter by the window.
s: The Spire is threatened with crumbling unless its restoration begins immediately, making it the Dean's principal creditor in his anxious reflections. Georgiana proposes using winnings from Dandy Dick's race to help pay for the Spire.

l: Durnstone Handicap, Dandy Dick, GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM enter by the window.
s: The handicap race is scheduled for the following day. Dandy Dick is considered a strong prospect despite odds of ten to one against him, while Blore claims that Bonny Betsy is bound to win.

l: gambling on horse races, Dandy Dick, GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM enter by the window.
s: Gambling on horse races becomes a possible solution to the Dean's financial problems when Georgiana urges him to stake fifty pounds on Dandy Dick. Blore reveals that he has previously gambled at races and accepts the Dean's money to place the wager.

l: the account for the fancy dresses, Dandy Dick, GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM enter by the window.
s: The Dean acknowledges that he has bills he intends to discharge when he can, but he lacks the money to settle them. Georgiana connects the bills with the need to raise funds for the threatened Spire.

l: the restoration of the Spire, Dandy Dick, GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM enter by the window.
s: The restoration of the Spire must begin immediately or the structure will crumble. The Dean lacks the required thousand pounds, and Georgiana proposes that a successful wager on Dandy Dick might provide money toward the restoration.

l: Dandy Dick, Dandy Dick, The curtains at the window are pushed aside, and SALOME and SHEBA enter; both in
s: Salome and Sheba return from the cancelled ball furious and complain about the Military, Nugent Darbey, and Gerald Tarver. Darbey and Tarver, disguised and shabby as Cavaliers, apologize and explain that the Military were summoned to St. Marvells, while Georgiana reprimands them for taking the girls out without permission. Salome and Sheba help Darbey and Tarver escape when Georgiana calls Sir Tristram to remove them. Hatcham then reports that the villain who set fire to the Swan Inn has been arrested while administering a dose to Dandy, and Blore identifies the prisoner as the Dean.

l: Salome, Dandy Dick, The curtains at the window are pushed aside, and SALOME and SHEBA enter; both in
s: Salome returns from the cancelled ball in a rage, lighting the candles and complaining about the cold, wet journey and the wasted expense. She and Sheba confront Darbey and Tarver, then help them escape when Georgiana calls Sir Tristram to remove them.

l: Sheba, Dandy Dick, The curtains at the window are pushed aside, and SALOME and SHEBA enter; both in
s: Sheba is angry that the ball was cancelled after she and Salome had endured the inconvenience of being wicked and rebellious. She joins Salome in confronting Darbey and Tarver and clings to Darbey's legs to prevent Sir Tristram from harming them.

l: Mr. Darbey, Dandy Dick, The curtains at the window are pushed aside, and SALOME and SHEBA enter; both in
s: Nugent Darbey appears in shabby Cavalier dress with Gerald Tarver and apologizes for the cancelled ball. He says that officers and gentlemen were responding to the sacred call of duty and claims that he and Tarver are guarding the ruins of the Swan Inn.

l: Major Tarver, Dandy Dick, The curtains at the window are pushed aside, and SALOME and SHEBA enter; both in
s: Gerald Tarver appears as a miserable, shabby Cavalier carrying a carriage umbrella. He explains that the Military were summoned to St. Marvells, asks Salome to smile on him again, and is helped to escape by Salome and Sheba.

l: Georgiana, Dandy Dick, The curtains at the window are pushed aside, and SALOME and SHEBA enter; both in
s: Georgiana scolds Salome and Sheba for going out without their aunt and reprimands Darbey and Tarver for encouraging the girls. She calls Sir Tristram to drive the outsiders into the road and opens the door when the gate bell rings.

l: Sir Tristram, Dandy Dick, The curtains at the window are pushed aside, and SALOME and SHEBA enter; both in
s: Sir Tristram appears after Georgiana calls him and is told to run Darbey and Tarver into the road. He twists Tarver's wig over his face and later questions Hatcham about the villain who set fire to the Swan Inn.

l: Hatcham, Dandy Dick, The curtains at the window are pushed aside, and SALOME and SHEBA enter; both in
s: Hatcham enters carrying a basin with the bolus and reports that the villain who set fire to the Swan Inn was caught while administering a dose to Dandy. He says the constable took the villain in a cart to the lock-up.

l: Dr. Jedd, Dandy Dick, The curtains at the window are pushed aside, and SALOME and SHEBA enter; both in
s: The Dean is identified by Blore as the villain who has been arrested after being caught administering a dose to Dandy.

l: the Military, Dandy Dick, The curtains at the window are pushed aside, and SALOME and SHEBA enter; both in
s: The Military were summoned to St. Marvells, preventing the ball from taking place. Darbey and Tarver say they were responding to the call of duty.

l: Durnstone Athenaeum, Dandy Dick, The curtains at the window are pushed aside, and SALOME and SHEBA enter; both in
s: The Durnstone Athenaeum is where Salome and Sheba arrived expecting the ball, only to find a notice on the front door announcing its cancellation.

l: the Swan Inn, Dandy Dick, The curtains at the window are pushed aside, and SALOME and SHEBA enter; both in
s: The Swan Inn has been reduced to ruins after being set on fire. Darbey and Tarver claim they are guarding its ruins.

l: Fancy Dress Masked Ball at Durnstone, Dandy Dick, The curtains at the window are pushed aside, and SALOME and SHEBA enter; both in
s: The ball is cancelled because the Military were summoned to St. Marvells. Salome and Sheba arrive at the Durnstone Athenaeum to find the cancellation notice and are jeered at by boys.

l: the fire at the Swan Inn, Dandy Dick, The curtains at the window are pushed aside, and SALOME and SHEBA enter; both in
s: The fire at the Swan Inn is attributed to a villain whom Hatcham reports has been caught and taken to the lock-up.

l: the military summons to St. Marvells, Dandy Dick, The curtains at the window are pushed aside, and SALOME and SHEBA enter; both in
s: The military summons to St. Marvells causes the Military to leave or be summoned away, resulting in the cancellation of the ball.

l: the arrest of the Dean, Dandy Dick, The curtains at the window are pushed aside, and SALOME and SHEBA enter; both in
s: The arrest of the Dean occurs after he is caught while administering a dose to Dandy. He is taken in a cart to the lock-up.

l: the notice cancelling the ball, Dandy Dick, The curtains at the window are pushed aside, and SALOME and SHEBA enter; both in
s: The notice cancelling the ball is posted on the front door of the Durnstone Athenaeum and reads, "Ball knocked on the head--Vivat Regina."

l: Dandy Dick, Dandy Dick, The curtains at the window are pushed aside, and SALOME and SHEBA enter; both in
s: Dandy is the horse to which the arrested villain was administering a dose. Georgiana and Sir Tristram react with alarm at the report that Dandy was being nobbled.

l: the Bolus, Dandy Dick, The curtains at the window are pushed aside, and SALOME and SHEBA enter; both in
s: The dose for Dandy is carried in a basin by Hatcham. The Dean is caught in the act of administering it to Dandy.

l: Dandy Dick, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: At the St. Marvells police station, Hannah Topping learns that the prisoner Noah Topping arrested is the Dean, her former master from the Deanery. She frees the Dean from the prisoner's cell and feeds him while proposing an escape during the journey to Durnstone, but Noah returns unexpectedly and discovers them together. Noah locks the Dean back in the cell and adds charges involving Hannah and his midday meal to the existing allegations.

l: Hannah Topping, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: Hannah cooks at the St. Marvells police station and learns that the prisoner is the Dean, her former master. She unlocks the prisoner's cell, feeds him, and gives him a plan involving old Nick, the cart, handcuffs, a duplicate key, and a whistle. Noah discovers them, and Hannah's attempt to help the Dean ends with him locked back in the cell.

l: Noah Topping, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: Noah is the Head Constable at St. Marvells and plans to take the prisoner to Durnstone after dinner, stopping to glimpse the racing. He is jealous and threatens Hannah's male friends, returns unexpectedly to the station, discovers the Dean with Hannah, and locks the Dean back in the cell. He says he will add charges of alienating Hannah's affections and embezzling his midday meal.

l: Dr. Jedd, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: The Dean is being held as the unidentified prisoner after being found in the Deanery stables. Hannah recognizes him, releases him from the cell, and feeds him, but he refuses her escape plan because of his conscience and concern for his dignity. Noah catches him and returns him to the cell.

l: Blore, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: Edward Blore visits Hannah at the police station from the Deanery. He is troubled because the prisoner is connected with his master and worries about the effect of the case on the Dean and on Dandy Dick.

l: St. Marvells, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: St. Marvells is where the police station is located and where Noah has recently become Head Constable. It is described as a place that returns a Conservative and as having a small class of expected offenders.

l: Durnstone, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: Durnstone is the destination to which Noah plans to take the prisoner after dinner. Hannah says its Superintendent, John Ruggles, and Inspectors Whitaker and Parker, together with their families, are chapel folk.

l: the Deanery, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: The Deanery is the Dean's home and the place where Hannah formerly worked as cook for seven years. The Dean's household has sent Blore to inquire about the arrest, and Blore says he will report Noah's intended visit.

l: the police station, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: The police station is a country station in St. Marvells, partly furnished as a kitchen and containing official police documents and implements. Hannah cooks there, Noah works there, and the Dean is held there before his planned transfer to Durnstone.

l: the prisoner's cell, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: The prisoner's cell, called the Strong-box in St. Marvells, is entered through a massive door with a wicket and iron grating. Hannah unlocks it with a duplicate key to release the Dean, and Noah later locks the Dean inside again.

l: the arrested man, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: The arrested man is described in the official book as a person found trespassing in the Deanery stables who refuses to give his name or any account of himself. He is the Dean, though Noah initially does not recognize him.

l: the arrest of the Dean, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: The arrest took place the previous night after the Dean was found in the Deanery stables. The prisoner is to be lodged at St. Marvells only overnight under the usual rule, then taken to Durnstone.

l: the journey to Durnstone, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: Noah intends to drive the Dean to Durnstone after dinner, using old Nick and passing the edge of the hill to get a glimpse of the racing. Hannah plans for the Dean to escape from the moving cart in Pear Tree Lane, but the plan is not carried out in this unit.

l: crime, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: Hannah says that crime levels everyone and believes the Dean's first offence merits giving him another start in life. The Dean insists that he is legally innocent, though he admits to a temporary moral aberration.

l: the alleged trespassing and attempted larceny, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: The official record states that the prisoner was found trespassing in the Deanery stables with intent, while Hannah refers to the expected case as petty larceny. The text does not establish that an attempted larceny was proved.

l: old Nick, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: Old Nick is the horse Noah plans to use for the journey to Durnstone. Hannah calls him vicious, while Noah says he can take the cart to the edge of the hill quickly; she explains that his former service in the Durnstone Fire Brigade makes him responsive to a double whistle.

l: Noah's cart, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: The cart is the vehicle in which Noah plans to take the Dean to Durnstone. Hannah's escape plan requires the Dean to jump from it, roll clear of the wheel, and use the whistle while old Nick runs on.

l: the handcuffs, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: Noah selects and examines a pair of handcuffs before preparing to take the prisoner to Durnstone. Hannah gives the Dean a small key that will unlock them once he is free from Noah.

l: the duplicate key, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: Hannah produces a duplicate key to the Strong-box and uses it to unlock the cell door. She later gives the Dean a small key intended to unlock his handcuffs during the planned escape.

l: the Dean's whistle, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: Hannah gives the Dean a whistle and tells him to blow once in Pear Tree Lane and again after jumping from the cart. She says old Nick will respond to the familiar double-whistle signal from his time in the Durnstone Fire Brigade.

l: the joint, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: The joint is Hannah's cooked meal and Noah's favorite dish. The Dean eats it after escaping from the cell, and Noah treats his eating of it as the embezzling of his midday meal.

l: the Dean's dignity, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: The Dean calls his dignity a priceless possession of man's middle age. He refuses to notify the Deanery because appearing in the police records and returning publicly would seriously impair it.

l: Hannah's cooking, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: Hannah's cooking is presented as a source of comfort and leverage. The Dean recognizes her culinary skill, eats the joint she prepares, and admits that if every mouthful could carry him back an hour he would finish it.

l: the attempted escape plan, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: Hannah's plan is for the Dean to travel with Noah in the cart, wait until Pear Tree Lane, blow the whistle, jump out, and use the handcuff key after Noah and old Nick continue toward Durnstone. The Dean rejects the plan, and Noah's return prevents it from being attempted.

l: the charge of alienating Hannah's affections, Dandy Dick, THE THIRD ACT.
s: Noah threatens to add a charge of alienating Hannah's affections to the charges already standing against the Dean. He makes the threat after finding the Dean being served Hannah's cooking.

l: Dandy Dick, Dandy Dick, [_HANNAH unlocks the door, and admits GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM, both dressed f
s: Georgiana Tidman and Sir Tristram visit the police-station to report that Augustin Jedd, the Dean of St. Marvells, has disappeared. Noah initially theorizes that the Dean committed suicide, but Georgiana recognizes him as the man arrested for dosing Dandy Dick and discovers him in the cell. The Dean says he was treating a suffering horse for chills, while Hannah secretly arranges his escape and warns that another charge threatens him. Noah takes the Dean toward Durnstone, but Hannah discovers that Noah has put Kitty in the cart and left Old Nick behind.

l: Georgiana, Dandy Dick, [_HANNAH unlocks the door, and admits GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM, both dressed f
s: Georgiana visits the police-station with Sir Tristram to report her brother Augustin Jedd's disappearance. She recognizes the Dean in the cell, seeks his release, and is told by Hannah that a whistle and Nick the fire-brigade horse will bring him safely back to the Deanery; she is then distressed to learn that Noah has taken Kitty instead of Old Nick.

l: Sir Tristram, Dandy Dick, [_HANNAH unlocks the door, and admits GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM, both dressed f
s: Sir Tristram accompanies Georgiana to the police-station and dictates a description of the missing Dean. After learning that the Dean is in the cell, he tells Noah to release him and helps Georgiana plan his escape.
